title: Regular functions under a regular point blowup
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian regular scheme of dimension at most two [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $x\in T$ be a reduced closed point and let $b:W=\operatorname{Bl}_xT\to T$ be its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Assume that the fibre $b^{-1}(x)$ is nonempty. The canonical morphism of sheaves of rings $\beta:\mathcal O_T\to b_*\mathcal O_W$ is an isomorphism. Explicitly, for every open $U\subseteq T$, the pullback $\beta_U:\mathcal O_T(U)\to\mathcal O_W(b^{-1}U)$ is an isomorphism, compatibly with restriction [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0AGS (lemma-cohomology-of-blowup), clause (4) at n=0: for a regular local ring A of dimension 2, the blowup X of A in its maximal ideal has H^0(X,O_X)=A. The stalk of b_*O_W at x is identified with these global sections by flat base change along Spec O_{T,x} -> T (coherent.tex Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology); when O_{T,x} has dimension 1 it is a discrete valuation ring (algebra.tex Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr), the centre is invertible near x and b is an isomorphism; dimension 0 gives an empty fibre and is excluded by hypothesis. Away from x, b is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the local chart package to $T,x,b$. It supplies $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the proper morphism $f:b^{-1}V\to V$, and the regular local domain $A=\mathcal O_{T,x}$ with $d\in\{0,1,2\}$. Proper means separated and finite type, so $f$ is quasi-compact and, by separatedness, quasi-separated. The localized scheme $Z$ is the maximal-ideal affine blowup over $A$, with the same coefficient maps and closed fibre.

source.place: Tags 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine) and 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up); algebra.tex Tags 00NP and 00NQ; resolve.tex Tag 0AGS, first proof paragraph (two-chart cover)

proof.text: For every $y\in V$, the neighbourhoods contained in $V$ are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of $y$, and inverse images of these opens under $f$ and $b$ coincide. Thus the stalk map for the restricted morphism $f$ identifies with $\beta_y$. Apply the qcqs functions local comparison to $f$ at $x$: it identifies $\beta_x:A\to(b_*\mathcal O_W)_x$ with the coefficient map $A\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ as a ring homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, i=0; localization and elementary fraction/germ comparison, followed by the germ-and-gluing argument for sheaf invertibility

proof.text: If $d=0$, the local chart package makes $Z$ empty, so its closed fibre is empty, contradicting the nonempty-fibre assumption. If $d=1$, the package says that the structural map $q:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ itself is an isomorphism. Pullback by its inverse gives an inverse to $q^\sharp:A=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, by functoriality. This is precisely the coefficient map identified in step 2. If $d=2$, its two charts embed as $A$-subalgebras of $A_s,A_t$, for a nonzero regular sequence $s,t$, and equal restrictions have equal images in $A_{st}$. The regular-sequence two-chart functions theorem therefore makes $A\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ an isomorphism. Thus $\beta_x$ is an isomorphism in all permitted cases.

source.place: Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers); two-chart divisibility and sheaf gluing argument for resolve.tex Tag 0AGS(4), n=0, generalized to an arbitrary two-chart A-scheme

proof.text: Put $E=T\setminus\{x\}$. The blowup-complement theorem makes $b$ an isomorphism over $E$, so $\beta_y$ is invertible for $y\ne x$. For $f:b^{-1}V\to V$, the qcqs comparison identifies every local coefficient map with $\beta_y$ by step 2; these are invertible at $x$ by step 3 and elsewhere by the complement. Its criterion therefore makes $\beta|_V$ invertible, while $\beta|_E$ is invertible by the blowup isomorphism. For an arbitrary open $U$ and $w\in\mathcal O_W(b^{-1}U)$, invert the restrictions of $w$ on $U\cap V$ and $U\cap E$. The resulting sections agree on $U\cap V\cap E$: their images there both equal the restriction of $w$, and $\beta$ is injective there. Glue them to $a\in\mathcal O_T(U)$. Its image is $w$ by sheaf uniqueness on the inverse-image cover. The same two-open cover proves injectivity of $\beta_U$. Thus every $\beta_U$ is a ring isomorphism; cancellation in its naturality squares makes the inverses compatible with restriction.
